questions.question: What does 'spouse reasoning' add to a family graph that basic parent-child and sibling links don't capture?
options: Nothing new
The marriage link connecting two people as husband and wife, which is needed to correctly trace in-law and combined-family relations
It replaces the need for generation tracking
It only applies to grandparents
questions.rationale: Spouse (marriage) links are a separate relationship type from parent-child and sibling links, and are needed to correctly trace relationships that go through marriage, like in-laws.

questions.question: What distinguishes the 'maternal side' from the 'paternal side' of a family?
options: Maternal side traces through the mother's relatives; paternal side traces through the father's relatives
They are the same thing
Maternal side only includes sisters
Paternal side only includes uncles
questions.rationale: The maternal side of a family traces relatives through one's mother's line, while the paternal side traces relatives through one's father's line.

questions.question: In an ambiguous blood relation problem where a person's gender isn't explicitly stated, how can it sometimes be inferred?
options: It can never be inferred
From gendered relation terms used elsewhere in the statement (like 'her son' or 'his daughter')
By assuming everyone is male by default
By counting the number of siblings
questions.rationale: Gendered terms referring to a person elsewhere in the statement, such as pronouns or relation words like 'his'/'her', can be used to infer that person's gender even if not stated directly.

questions.question: What does 'relationship composition' mean in blood relation reasoning?
options: Combining two or more known direct relations to derive a new, indirect relation between two people
Drawing a family tree with colors
Listing every person's name alphabetically
Ignoring intermediate relationships entirely
questions.rationale: Relationship composition is the process of chaining known direct relations (e.g., 'mother' + 'sister') to derive the indirect relation between two people who aren't directly connected in the statement.

questions.question: If P is Q's mother, and Q is R's sister, what is P to R?
options: P is R's mother
P is R's aunt
P is R's grandmother
P is R's sister
questions.rationale: Since Q is R's sister, Q and R share the same mother — so P, being Q's mother, is also R's mother.

questions.question: What is 'contradiction detection' used for when building a family graph from a multi-statement problem?
options: It has no practical use
Catching a new statement that conflicts with relationships already established, signalling an error in the assumed structure
Automatically solving the problem without reading it
Detecting spelling mistakes
questions.rationale: As you add each statement to the family graph, checking for contradictions against already-established links catches invalid assumptions before they propagate further errors.

questions.question: Why might a blood relation problem describe an 'unknown relation' rather than stating it directly?
options: To make the puzzle unsolvable
To require the solver to derive the exact relation through composition of the stated direct links
Because unknown relations are never asked about
Because it is a typo in the question
questions.rationale: Many blood relation questions deliberately withhold the final relation, requiring you to derive it by composing the direct relationships given in the statements.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'symbolic representation' (e.g., using compact notation for relations) in solving complex blood relation problems?
options: It has no purpose beyond appearance
It compresses verbose relation statements into a compact, unambiguous notation that's easier to trace and compose
It replaces the need for a family tree entirely
It only works for two-person problems
questions.rationale: Symbolic notation lets you write multi-statement problems compactly and trace/compose relations more reliably than re-reading full sentences repeatedly, especially in longer chains.

questions.question: What does building a 'Blood Relation AST' (structured representation) allow you to do?
options: Nothing useful for solving
Represent the parsed statements as a structured internal model that can be queried and reasoned over systematically, rather than re-reading prose each time
Replace all family terms with numbers only
Only applies to computer programs, not to solving by hand
questions.rationale: Structuring the parsed relationships into an internal model lets you query and compose relations systematically instead of repeatedly re-reading and re-interpreting the original prose.

questions.question: In relationship composition, why does the order in which you chain relations matter?
options: It never matters
Composing relations in the wrong order can produce an entirely different (and incorrect) final relationship
Order only matters for spouse links
Order only matters in circular arrangements, not blood relations
questions.rationale: Relationship composition is directional — chaining 'mother of' then 'sister of' gives a different result than 'sister of' then 'mother of', so preserving the correct order is essential to deriving the right final relation.
